# EveryWare UI: every component, for a program that writes harry apps

One section per component, the same text as docs/ai/<component>.md: Figma set and variants, the parts the code sets, transitions, the Rust API, the four lines the app writes, the guide. The principles and rules: docs/llms.txt.

## #button

A tappable text button, Material 3's filled, tonal and text button, in two widths.

### Figma

- set: `#button` (node 2-9 in the Library)
- property `kind`: `primary` | `secondary` | `ghost`
- property `state`: `default` | `disabled`
- property `size`: `regular` | `compact`
- variant string: `kind=primary, state=default, size=regular` (the properties in this order; `Button::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: #button/pressed opacity (pressed): set by code, not a variant; size: the design's width (200, 116), the label centred
- nodes set by code (`Button`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#button/label`, `#button/pressed`
- on the screens now: `#wifi/cancel` in #wifi-content (step=networks) (node 3-6); `#wifi/rescan` in #wifi-content (step=networks) (node 3-18); `#wifi/connect` in #wifi-content (step=password) (node 3-28); `#intercom/talk` in #smarthome-root (node 1-251)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#button` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/button.rs`, type `Button`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Button`)
- `pub fn new(kind: ButtonKind, label: impl Into<String>) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<ButtonEvent>`
- events `ButtonEvent`: `Clicked`
- pub enum `ButtonKind`: The kind property of #button.
  - `Primary`: Filled with the accent colour: the main action.
  - `Secondary`: Soft fill.
  - `Ghost`: Text only.
- pub enum `ButtonSize`: The size property of #button and #icon-button: the size is the design's, as Google's components are drawn (a fixed size per variant, the label centred in it), not the label's.
  - `Regular`: #button 200 wide (a sheet's Connect, Cancel); #icon-button 56.
  - `Compact`: #button 116 wide (Talk in a widget's row); #icon-button 48.
- pub struct `Button`: A button with text.
  - field `pub kind: ButtonKind`: Which look.
  - field `pub size: ButtonSize`: Which width.
  - field `pub label: String`: The text on it.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Pressed and disabled.
  - `pub fn compact(mut self) -> Self`: The same button in the compact size.
- pub enum `ButtonEvent`: What a button reports.
  - `Clicked`: The button was tapped.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::button::{Button, ButtonEvent, ButtonKind};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub wifi_cancel: Button,
// wifi_cancel: Button::new(ButtonKind::Primary, "Talk").compact(),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
wifi_cancel: Slot = "#wifi/cancel" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.wifi_cancel = slot("#wifi/cancel", &state.wifi_cancel);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
"#wifi/cancel" => {
    if let Some(ButtonEvent::Clicked) = state.wifi_cancel.on(gesture) {
        // yours
    }
}
```

### Live: `#wifi/cancel` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// state.rs:144
pub cancel: Button,
cancel: Button::new(ButtonKind::Secondary, "Cancel"),

// ui_model.rs:214
wifi_cancel: Slot = "#wifi/cancel" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:66
model.wifi_cancel = slot("#wifi/cancel", &wifi.cancel);

// actions.rs:428
"#wifi/cancel" => {
    if wifi.cancel.on(gesture) == Some(ButtonEvent::Clicked) {
        match wifi.step {
            // from the password back to the list (as Android does)
            Step::Password => wifi.back_to_networks(),
            // the form closes with its transition
            Step::Networks => wifi.form.close(),
        }
    }
}
```

A button is the design's fixed size per variant (Google's components are drawn that way, the label centred in the box), not the label's width. `kind` is the look, `size` the width (200 regular for a sheet's actions, 116 compact in a widget's row), `state` only `default` or `disabled`: pressed is a layer the code fades, not a variant.

### In Figma
A button on a screen is a slot of the design's size: a frame 200 × 56 (`size=regular`) or 116 × 56 (`size=compact`) named `#<screen>/<name>` (for example `#wifi/connect`), with an instance of `#button` inside. The instance's label is the designer's preview; the app writes the real label into `#button/label`. Place two buttons as two slots, never one instance twice.

### In the app
```rust
// state: the component
pub connect: Button,                                    // Button::new(ButtonKind::Primary, "Connect")
pub talk: Button,                                       // Button::new(ButtonKind::Primary, "Talk").compact()

// ui_model: one Slot per place on the screen
wifi_connect: Slot = "#wifi/connect" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter: the slot gets the component (variant, label, pressed fade)
model.wifi_connect = slot("#wifi/connect", &wifi.connect);

// actions: the gesture harry reported for the node goes to the button; it answers Clicked
"#intercom/talk" => {
    if d.talk.on(gesture) == Some(ButtonEvent::Clicked) {
        log::info!("smarthome: Talk");
    }
}
```

Disable with `button.press.enabled = false` (the variant becomes `state=disabled`, never animated).

### Traps
- A label changed at runtime needs the text node named `#button/label` in every variant; a renamed inner layer is lost on a variant swap, a text override is kept.
- Two buttons on one screen must sit in two slots: harry finds parts by node name, and the slot gives each clone its own scope.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #icon-button

A tappable button with one glyph and no label, Material 3's icon button, in two sizes.

### Figma

- set: `#icon-button` (node 2-51 in the Library)
- property `kind`: `tonal` | `glass` | `scrim`
- property `state`: `default` | `disabled`
- property `icon`: `minus` | `plus` | `sliders-horizontal` | `maximize-2` | `chevron-right` | `settings-2` | `wifi` | `x` | `house` | `door-open` | `bed-double` | `armchair` | `droplets`
- property `size`: `regular` | `compact`
- variant string: `kind=tonal, state=default, icon=minus, size=regular` (the properties in this order; `IconButton::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: #icon-button/pressed opacity (pressed): set by code, not a variant; icon: the design's icons; size: 56, 48
- nodes set by code (`IconButton`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#icon-button/pressed`
- on the screens now: `#status/wifi` in #smarthome-root (node 4-64); `#climate/minus` in #overview (node 1-37); `#climate/plus` in #overview (node 1-43); `#climate/humidity-adjust` in #overview (node 1-55)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#icon-button` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/button.rs`, type `IconButton`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for IconButton`)
- `pub fn new(kind: IconButtonKind, icon: Icon) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<ButtonEvent>`
- events `ButtonEvent`: `Clicked`
- pub enum `IconButtonKind`: The kind property of #icon-button: the circle, as the dashboard draws it.
  - `Tonal`: Soft accent circle: the widgets' buttons.
  - `Glass`: White 44 % with a white line: the status row.
  - `Scrim`: White 15 %: over the camera.
- pub enum `Icon`: The icon property of #icon-button: the design's icons (lucide names).
  - `Minus`: `minus`
  - `Plus`: `plus`
  - `Sliders`: `sliders-horizontal`
  - `Maximize`: `maximize-2`
  - `ChevronRight`: `chevron-right`
  - `Settings`: `settings-2`
  - `Wifi`: `wifi`
  - `Close`: `x`: closes (a sheet)
  - `House`: `house`: home (a hub's rail)
  - `DoorOpen`: `door-open`: a door, the entrance
  - `BedDouble`: `bed-double`: a bedroom
  - `Armchair`: `armchair`: a living room
  - `Droplets`: `droplets`: humidity, water
- pub struct `IconButton`: A button with an icon. Its size is the design's (regular 56, compact 48).
  - field `pub kind: IconButtonKind`: Which look.
  - field `pub icon: Icon`: Which icon.
  - field `pub size: ButtonSize`: Which size.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Pressed and disabled.
  - `pub fn compact(mut self) -> Self`: The same button in the compact size.
- pub enum `ButtonEvent`: What a button reports.
  - `Clicked`: The button was tapped.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::button::{ButtonEvent, Icon, IconButton, IconButtonKind};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub status_wifi: IconButton,
// status_wifi: IconButton::new(IconButtonKind::Tonal, Icon::Plus),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
status_wifi: Slot = "#status/wifi" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.status_wifi = slot("#status/wifi", &state.status_wifi);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
"#status/wifi" => {
    if let Some(ButtonEvent::Clicked) = state.status_wifi.on(gesture) {
        // yours
    }
}
```

### Live: `#status/wifi` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// state.rs:28
pub wifi: WifiSheet,
wifi: IconButton::new(IconButtonKind::Glass, Icon::Wifi).compact(),

// ui_model.rs:160
wifi_indicator: Slot = "#status/wifi" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:29
model.wifi_indicator = slot("#status/wifi", &d.wifi);

// actions.rs:130
HomeAction::Gesture(node, gesture) if node == "#status/wifi" => {
    // the Wi-Fi indicator opens the sheet; the sheet starts over every time
    if state.dash.wifi.on(*gesture) == Some(ButtonEvent::Clicked) && !state.wifi.form.is_open() {
        state.wifi = WifiSheet::opened(state.wifi.networks.clone(), state.wifi.state.clone());
        house_link::send_wifi_command(wifi_scan());
    }
}
```

`kind` is the look (filled, tonal, plain), `icon` the design's glyph (Lucide names), `size` 56 or 48. `state` only `default` or `disabled`; pressed is `#icon-button/pressed`, a layer the code fades in. The glyph is part of the variant: an icon that changes at runtime is a variant change (rebuild), so pick a stable glyph per place, or stack glyphs in a slot of your own and light one by opacity.

### In Figma
A slot of the variant's size (56 × 56 or 48 × 48) named `#<screen>/<name>` (`#climate/plus`) with an instance of `#icon-button` inside; the instance's `icon` is the preview, the app's `IconButton::new(kind, icon)` picks the real one. A row of icon buttons is a row of slots, 8 px apart.

### Traps
- A glyph missing in the `icon` property of the set cannot be shown: `everyware_ui_test` names the variant; add the glyph to `components.json` and the generator (ui-component skill), do not draw it on the screen.
- The pressed layer is in the variant, not in the slot: a slot drawn by hand without an instance shows no press.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #toggle

An on/off switch, Material 3's switch: the value moves the thumb and fades the track, the variant is only the state.

### Figma

- set: `#toggle` (node 2-882 in the Library)
- property `state`: `default` | `pressed` | `disabled`
- variant string: `state=default` (the properties in this order; `Toggle::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: #toggle/thumb progress marker meter, #toggle/on opacity: set by code, not a variant
- nodes set by code (`Toggle`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#toggle/thumb`, `#toggle/on`
- on the screens now: `#wifi/reveal` in #wifi-content (step=password) (node 3-32); `#entryway/light` in Room controls (node 1-138)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#toggle` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out
- value: 200 ms ease-in-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/toggle.rs`, type `Toggle`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Toggle`)
- `pub fn new(value: bool) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<ToggleEvent>`
- events `ToggleEvent`: `Toggled(bool)`
- pub struct `Toggle`: An on/off switch.
  - field `pub value: bool`: On or off.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Pressed and disabled.
  - `pub fn set(&mut self, value: bool)`: Sets the value from outside (the device reported it).
  - `pub fn target(&self) -> f32`: Where the thumb and the blue track go: 0 (off) or 100 (on), for meter and opacity.
  - `pub fn value_transition(&self) -> Option<Transition>`: How the thumb and the track move to a new target.
- pub enum `ToggleEvent`: What a toggle reports.
  - `Toggled`: The user switched it; the new value.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::toggle::{Toggle, ToggleEvent};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub wifi_reveal: Toggle,
// wifi_reveal: Toggle::new(false),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
wifi_reveal: Slot = "#wifi/reveal" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.wifi_reveal = slot("#wifi/reveal", &state.wifi_reveal);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
"#wifi/reveal" => {
    if let Some(ToggleEvent::Toggled(on)) = state.wifi_reveal.on(gesture) {
        let _ = on; // yours: state.wifi_reveal.value is the same
    }
}
```

Read the value any time as `state.wifi_reveal.value` (a pub field); `state.wifi_reveal.set(on)` follows the device without a gesture.

### Live: `#wifi/reveal` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// state.rs:147
/// Show the password instead of dots.
pub reveal: Toggle,
reveal: Toggle::new(false),

// ui_model.rs:224
wifi_reveal: Slot = "#wifi/reveal" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:67
model.wifi_reveal = slot("#wifi/reveal", &wifi.reveal);

// actions.rs:444
"#wifi/reveal" => {
    if let Some(ToggleEvent::Toggled(shown)) = wifi.reveal.on(gesture) {
        wifi.password_mut().secure = !shown;
    }
}
```

`state` is `default`, `pressed` (the thumb stretches under the finger) or `disabled`. On and off are not variants: `#toggle/thumb` is a horizontal progress marker the code moves from 0 to 100, `#toggle/on` the blue track the code fades in, both display-only and animated by the `value` transition (200 ms). `Toggle::set(value)` follows the device without a gesture; `on(gesture)` answers `Toggled(bool)` on a completed tap.

### In Figma
A slot 52 × 32 named `#<screen>/<name>` (`#entryway/light`) with an instance of `#toggle` inside. The marker node sits at x = 0 of the track with its travel as startX..endX; the preview shows the off position.

### Traps
- On/off as a variant switches in steps and rebuilds the tree: keep the value on the marker and the opacity.
- Two toggles on one screen share the part names `#toggle/thumb`, `#toggle/on`: each in its own slot, or they move together.
- A toggle inside a list row switches instead of fading on stock harry (the animation pass read only the global scope): the display_safety series in `everyware/patches` fixes it.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #radio

A group of radio buttons where one option is on; the group owns the selection, each button is a variant.

### Figma

- set: `#radio` (node 2-898 in the Library)
- property `value`: `off` | `on`
- property `state`: `default` | `pressed` | `disabled`
- variant string: `value=off, state=default` (the properties in this order; `Radio::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- nodes set by code (`Radio`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#radio/label`
- on the screens now: not used yet
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#radio` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out
- value: 160 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/radio.rs`, type `Radio`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Radio`)
- events `RadioEvent`: `Selected(usize)`
- pub struct `Radio`: One radio button; part of a RadioGroup.
  - field `pub label: String`: The text next to it.
  - field `pub on: bool`: This option is the selected one.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Pressed and disabled.
- pub struct `RadioGroup`: A group of radio buttons with one selected.
  - field `pub options: Vec<Radio>`: The options, in order.
  - `pub fn selected(&self) -> Option<usize>`: The index of the selected option.
- pub enum `RadioEvent`: What a radio group reports.
  - `Selected`: The user picked the option with this index.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::radio::{RadioEvent, RadioGroup};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub home_radio: RadioGroup,
// home_radio: RadioGroup::new(["Off", "Low", "High"]),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
home_radio_1: Slot = "#home/radio/1" ["SlotCustomizer"];
home_radio_2: Slot = "#home/radio/2" ["SlotCustomizer"];
home_radio_3: Slot = "#home/radio/3" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.home_radio_1 = slot("#home/radio/1", &state.home_radio.options[0]);
model.home_radio_2 = slot("#home/radio/2", &state.home_radio.options[1]);
model.home_radio_3 = slot("#home/radio/3", &state.home_radio.options[2]);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
_ if node.starts_with("#home/radio/") => {
    // the option from its slot's name: #home/radio/1 is index 0
    if let Some(i) = row_of("#home/radio", node).and_then(|n| n.checked_sub(1)) {
        if let Some(RadioEvent::Selected(i)) = state.home_radio.on(i, gesture) {
            let _ = i; // yours
        }
    }
}
```

One slot per option, `#home/radio/1`, `#home/radio/2` ...; the group decides which is on.

`value` is `on` or `off`, `state` `default`, `pressed` or `disabled`. The group (`RadioGroup`) holds which index is selected and answers `Selected(index)`; each option is a `Radio` whose variant follows the group. Selection is a variant change (rare, a tap), so there is no meter here.

### In Figma
One slot per option, 24 × 24 (or the row that holds it) named `#<screen>/<group>/<i>`, each with an instance of `#radio`; the label is a text of the screen next to it, not part of the component. The group is the app's: the slots share nothing in Figma.

### Traps
- The index the app passes to `on(index, gesture)` comes from the node name (`#x/2`), not from the layer order: name the options in order.
- A label inside the component would need `#radio/label` in every variant; the design keeps labels on the screen.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #dropdown

A closed pill that opens a list of items below it; the open list and the selected item are opacities, the variant only the state.

### Figma

- set: `#dropdown` (node 2-924 in the Library)
- property `state`: `default` | `disabled`
- variant string: `state=default` (the properties in this order; `Dropdown::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: #dropdown/list opacity (open), #dropdown/item/N/selected opacity: set by code, not a variant
- nodes set by code (`Dropdown`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#dropdown/value`, `#dropdown/list`, `#dropdown/item/{}`, `#dropdown/item/<…>`
- on the screens now: `#status/presence` in #smarthome-root (node 1-18)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#dropdown` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- open: 200 ms ease-out
- close: 150 ms ease-in
- select: 150 ms ease-in

### Rust

- module: `core/src/dropdown.rs`, type `Dropdown`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Dropdown`)
- `pub fn new<S: Into<String>>(items: impl IntoIterator<Item = S>) -> Self`
- events `DropdownEvent`: `Selected(usize)`
- pub struct `Dropdown`: A dropdown with its items.
  - field `pub items: Vec<String>`: The items of the list.
  - field `pub selected: usize`: Index of the selected item.
  - field `pub open: bool`: The list is shown.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Disabled (the field opens on tap, pressed is not shown).
  - `pub fn value(&self) -> &str`: The text shown in the field.
  - `pub fn on_field(&mut self, gesture: Gesture)`: Applies a gesture on the field: a tap opens or closes the list.
  - `pub fn on_item(&mut self, index: usize, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<DropdownEvent>`: Applies a gesture on item `index`: a tap on the open list selects it and closes. Taps on the closed (transparent) list are ignored.
  - `pub fn close(&mut self)`: Closes the list without a choice (a tap outside).
  - `pub fn list_target(&self) -> f32`: Opacity target of the list: 100 open, 0 closed.
  - `pub fn mark_target(&self, index: usize) -> f32`: Opacity target of the selection mark of item `index`.
  - `pub fn list_transition(&self) -> Option<Transition>`: How the list fades: open and close have their own curves.
- pub enum `DropdownEvent`: What a dropdown reports.
  - `Selected`: The user picked the item with this index.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::dropdown::{Dropdown, DropdownEvent};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub status_presence: Dropdown,
// status_presence: Dropdown::new(["At home", "Away", "Asleep"]),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
status_presence: Slot = "#status/presence" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.status_presence = slot("#status/presence", &state.status_presence);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
"#status/presence" => state.status_presence.on_field(gesture),
// the open list's items report by their own names, #dropdown/item/1 ...
_ if node.starts_with("#dropdown/item/") => {
    let n = node["#dropdown/item/".len()..].parse::<usize>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_sub(1));
    if let Some(DropdownEvent::Selected(i)) = n.and_then(|n| state.status_presence.on_item(n, gesture)) {
        let _ = i; // yours
    }
}
```

The field opens and closes the list (`on_field`); an item reports by its own name, one open list at a time.

### Live: `#status/presence` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// state.rs:76
/// Status row: who is home, and the Wi-Fi indicator that opens the sheet.
pub presence: Dropdown,
presence: Dropdown::new(["At home", "Away", "Asleep"]),

// ui_model.rs:159
presence: Slot = "#status/presence" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:26
model.presence = slot("#status/presence", &d.presence);

// actions.rs:297
"#status/presence" => d.presence.on_field(gesture),
```

`state` is `default` or `disabled`. Open is `#dropdown/list` faded in, the chosen row `#dropdown/item/N/selected` lit, both display-only. The pill shows the selected item's text (`#dropdown/value`); the items report taps by their own names (`#dropdown/item/2`), unambiguous while one dropdown is open on the screen. `on_field(gesture)` opens and closes, `on_item(i, gesture)` answers `Selected(i)`.

### In Figma
The slot keeps the closed pill's height (48) and lets the list hang below it (counter-align MIN, no clipping on the slot), so a row of the dashboard does not grow by the open list. The component is drawn as tall as its open list.

### Traps
- A slot as tall as the component centres the pill half above the row (seen after a regenerate): slot height = the pill, `frameMaskDisabled` on the slot.
- Items are a fixed number in the set (the list is drawn); more items than rows are not shown. The app fills the texts, it cannot add rows.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #list-item

One row of a list, Material 3's list item, with a leading icon or image, a headline, supporting text and a trailing end; rows live in a ListView.

### Figma

- set: `#list-item` (node 2-1133 in the Library)
- property `state`: `default` | `selected` | `disabled`
- property `kind`: `plain` | `icon` | `image` | `toggle` | `chevron` | `text`
- property `lines`: `one` | `two` | `three`
- property `size`: `regular` | `column` | `wide`
- variant string: `state=default, kind=plain, lines=one, size=regular` (the properties in this order; `ListItem::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: the roles of Material 3's list item: #list-item/title (headline), /subtitle (supporting text, not in lines one), #list-item/pressed opacity (pressed): set by code. Slots #list-item/leading (kind icon) and #list-item/trailing (kinds plain, icon): instances of #icon, the glyph set by code, the trailing one shown or hidden. Kind image: #list-item/image (a picture the app registered, set by code) and #list-item/trailing-text. Kind text: a label (#list-item/title) and its value (#list-item/trailing-text, right aligned), lines one only. lines: one and two (72) for the kinds plain, icon, toggle and chevron, two and three (128, headline and supporting text up to two lines each) for image. Rows of a scrolling list (ListView, harry glue list()): a clipping slot, rows pitch apart, drag/fling as Android
- nodes set by code (`ListRow`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#list-item/title`, `#list-item/subtitle`, `#list-item/trailing-text`, `#list-item/image`, `#list-item/{slot}/{glyph}`, `#list-item/pressed`, `#list-item/{slot}/<…>`
- on the screens now: `#wifi/networks` in #wifi-content (step=networks) (node 3-9); `#news/list` in #overview (node 4-85); `#automations/routines` in #automations-screen (state=hidden) (node 5-111); `#device/state-list` in #device-content (state=default) (node 6-15)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#list-item` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out
- select: 160 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/list_item.rs`, type `ListItem`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for ListRow`)
- `pub fn new(kind: ListItemKind, title: impl Into<String>, subtitle: impl Into<String>) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<ListItemEvent>`
- events `ListItemEvent`: `Clicked`
- pub enum `ListItemKind`: The kind property of #list-item: what is at the ends of the row.
  - `Plain`: Text only.
  - `Icon`: An icon before the text.
  - `Toggle`: A toggle at the end.
  - `Chevron`: A chevron at the end: opens something.
  - `Image`: An image before the text (a registered picture, everyware_ui::images) and a trailing text at the end.
  - `Text`: A label and its value (the trailing supporting text of Material 3) at the end, in one line: "Firmware · 0.1.0".
- pub enum `ListItemLines`: The lines property of #list-item: the height of the row.
  - `One`: The headline only (72, the touch target).
  - `Two`: Headline and one line of supporting text (72).
  - `Three`: Headline and supporting text up to two lines each (128); with an image only.
- pub enum `ListItemSize`: The size property of #list-item: the width of the row (a variant has a fixed size).
  - `Regular`: 440 wide: a column of a card.
  - `Column`: 490 wide: a column of a dashboard.
  - `Wide`: 960 wide: a sheet's list.
- pub struct `ListItem`: A row of a list.
  - field `pub kind: ListItemKind`: What is at the ends of the row.
  - field `pub title: String`: First line.
  - field `pub subtitle: String`: Second line.
  - field `pub selected: bool`: Marked as the current one.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Pressed and disabled.
  - field `pub leading: Option<&'static str>`: The glyph of `#icon` in the leading slot (kind icon), by its `icon` value.
  - field `pub trailing: Option<&'static str>`: The glyph of `#icon` in the trailing slot (kinds plain and icon); None hides it.
  - field `pub size: ListItemSize`: The width.
  - field `pub lines: ListItemLines`: The height.
  - field `pub image: Option<String>`: The picture of kind image: the key of a registered image; None keeps the placeholder.
  - field `pub trailing_text: String`: The trailing text of kinds image (a source, an age) and text (the value).
  - `pub fn leading(mut self, icon: &'static str) -> Self`: The leading icon (kind icon): a glyph of `#icon`.
  - `pub fn trailing(mut self, icon: Option<&'static str>) -> Self`: The trailing icon: a glyph of `#icon`, or none.
  - `pub fn wide(mut self) -> Self`: The wide row (960).
  - `pub fn size(mut self, size: ListItemSize) -> Self`: The width.
  - `pub fn lines(mut self, lines: ListItemLines) -> Self`: The height.
  - `pub fn image(mut self, key: impl Into<String>) -> Self`: The picture (kind image): the key of a registered image.
  - `pub fn trailing_text(mut self, text: impl Into<String>) -> Self`: The trailing text (kinds image and text).
  - `pub fn set_selected(&mut self, selected: bool)`: Marks or unmarks the row as the selected one.
- pub enum `ListItemEvent`: What a list item reports.
  - `Clicked`: The row was tapped.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::list_item::{ListItem, ListItemKind};
use everyware_ui::list_view::{ListEvent, ListView};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub wifi_networks: ListView,
// wifi_networks: ListView::new([ListItem::new(ListItemKind::Plain, "Title", "Supporting text")], 744.0, 72.0 + 8.0),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
wifi_networks: Slot = "#wifi/networks" interactive ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.wifi_networks = list("#wifi/networks", &state.wifi_networks);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
// the list itself (a drag between rows) or a row, "#wifi/networks/<row>"
_ if node == "#wifi/networks" || node.starts_with("#wifi/networks/") => {
    if let Some(ListEvent::Chosen(row)) = state.wifi_networks.on(row_of("#wifi/networks", node), gesture, Instant::now()) {
        let _ = row; // yours
    }
}
```

A list is a `ListView` of rows (`ListItem`), its slot `interactive`; new rows with `state.wifi_networks.set_rows(...)` keep a tap in progress.

### Live: `#wifi/networks` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// state.rs:141
/// The list #wifi/networks: one row (ui-lib list item) per network, scrolling.
pub list: ListView,
list: ListView::new([], LIST_H, ROW_PITCH),

// ui_model.rs:217
wifi_networks: Slot = "#wifi/networks" interactive ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:61
model.wifi_networks = list("#wifi/networks", &wifi.list);
```

`kind` is what the row carries: `plain`, `icon` (a leading glyph), `image` (a leading picture), `toggle`, `chevron`, `text` (a value on the right, for label and value rows). `lines` one to three, `size` the width (`regular`, `column` 490 for two columns in a dialog, `wide` 960). `state` only `default`, `selected`, `disabled`: pressed is a layer.

Rows do not stand alone on a screen: a **ListView** (`core/src/list_view.rs`) holds them, scrolls them (drag, fling, Android's physics), selects one and reports a tap; the slot of the list is a clipping frame with preview rows, harry places the rows at their scrolled y.

### In Figma
A list is one slot for all its rows: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` (for example `#wifi/networks`) as wide as a row (`size=wide` 960, `column` 490) and as high as the rows it shows, with **Clip content** on, and inside it as many preview instances of `#list-item` as fit, one row pitch apart (72 high, 8 between: 80). harry places the real rows at their scrolled position; the preview rows only show the designer the list. The scrollbar is a slot of its own beside the list (`#<screen>/<name>-scrollbar`, an instance of `#scrollbar` of the list's height), not inside it.

### In the app
```rust
// state: the rows and the view (height of the slot, pitch between rows)
pub list: ListView,                                     // ListView::new([], LIST_H, ROW_PITCH)
fn row(network: &Network) -> ListItem {
    ListItem::new(ListItemKind::Icon, network.ssid.clone(), network.security.name()).wide().leading("wifi").trailing(Some("lock"))
}
list.set_rows(networks.iter().map(row));                // keeps pressed and selected by key

// ui_model: the list slot is interactive (a drag may start between the rows), the scrollbar is not
wifi_networks: Slot = "#wifi/networks" interactive ["SlotCustomizer"];
wifi_scrollbar: Slot = "#wifi/scrollbar" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter
model.wifi_networks = list("#wifi/networks", &wifi.list);
model.wifi_scrollbar = scrollbar("#wifi/scrollbar", &wifi.list);

// actions: a gesture on a row ("#wifi/networks/3") or on the list itself (None: between the rows)
if node == "#wifi/networks" || node.starts_with("#wifi/networks/") {
    let row = node.strip_prefix("#wifi/networks/").and_then(|r| r.parse().ok());
    if let Some(ListEvent::Chosen(row)) = wifi.list.on(row, gesture, Instant::now()) {
        // the user tapped row `row`
    }
}
```

### Traps
- A glyph per row is not a variant (harry does not swap a variant inside a list item): every glyph of the stack is in the row at opacity 0 and `leading(icon)` lights one.
- Rows replaced while a finger is down: `set_rows` carries pressed and selected over by the row's key, so the tap still lands.
- The scrollbar is its own slot beside the list; inside the list it would scroll away with the rows.

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #scrollbar

The thumb of a scrolling list: a vertical progress marker along a track, faded in while the list moves.

### Figma

- set: `#scrollbar` (node 2-1121 in the Library)
- property `length`: `472` | `744`
- variant string: `length=472` (the properties in this order; `ListView::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: the thumb of a scrolling list: #scrollbar/thumb vertical progress marker (0..100 along the track), the clone fades out 300 ms after the content stopped (transition hide); one value of length per list height in the design
- on the screens now: `#wifi/scrollbar` in #wifi-content (step=networks) (node 3-16); `#news/scrollbar` in #overview (node 4-92); `#automations/routines-scrollbar` in #automations-screen (state=hidden) (node 5-118); `#device/state-list-scrollbar` in #device-content (state=default) (node 6-22)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#scrollbar` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- hide: 250 ms ease-in

### Rust

- module: `core/src/list_view.rs`, type `ListView`
- `pub fn new(rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = R>, view_h: f32, pitch: f32) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, row: Option<usize>, gesture: Gesture, now: Instant) -> Option<ListEvent>`
- events `ListEvent`: `Chosen(usize)`
- pub struct `ListView`: A scrolling list of rows (`#list-item` by default, any `Row`).
  - `pub fn horizontal(mut self) -> Self`: The same list, scrolling sideways: rows left to right, the finger's x moves it, `view_h` is the slot's width and `pitch` a row's width plus gap.
  - `pub fn is_horizontal(&self) -> bool`: Whether the rows lie side by side.
  - `pub fn rows(&self) -> &[R]`: The rows, in order.
  - `pub fn row_mut(&mut self, row: usize) -> Option<&mut R>`: A row to change.
  - `pub fn set_rows(&mut self, rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = R>)`: Replaces the rows (a new scan). A row with the same key keeps its pressed and selected state, so a tap in progress survives a refresh between its down and its up (a list fed by a topic refreshes at any moment); the scroll stays within the content.
  - `pub fn pitch(&self) -> f32`: The row pitch (height plus gap).
  - `pub fn view_h(&self) -> f32`: The viewport's height.
  - `pub fn scroll(&self) -> Scroll`: Where the content is (for the harry glue, which steps a fling itself).
  - `pub fn scroll_at(&self, now: Instant) -> f32`: The scroll at `now`.
  - `pub fn content_h(&self) -> f32`: The content's height (rows times pitch; the gap after the last row stays).
  - `pub fn max_scroll(&self) -> f32`: How far the content scrolls at most.
  - `pub fn thumb(&self, now: Instant) -> f32`: The scrollbar's thumb: where (0..100) along the track; 0 when nothing scrolls.
  - `pub fn selected(&self) -> Option<usize>`: The selected row.
  - `pub fn select(&mut self, row: Option<usize>)`: Marks a row as the selected one (none: clears the mark).

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::list_view::ListView;

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
wifi_scrollbar: Slot = "#wifi/scrollbar" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action

// actions.rs: nothing, display only
```

Display only: it follows the `ListView` of its list (`list`) and fades out when the list stops.

### Live: `#wifi/scrollbar` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// state.rs:141

list: ListView::new([], LIST_H, ROW_PITCH),

// ui_model.rs:221

```

`length` is the thumb's share of the track, as the design draws it; the position `#scrollbar/thumb` is a vertical progress marker (0..100) the code moves with the list's scroll. The scrollbar has no state of its own: `scrollbar("#x", &list)` reads the `ListView` of the rows and fades the thumb out after the list settles.

### In Figma
A slot of the list's height, 8 wide, beside the list's slot (not inside it: inside, it would scroll away with the rows), named `#<screen>/<name>-scrollbar`, with an instance of `#scrollbar` of that height.

### Traps
- A scrollbar inside the list's slot scrolls with the content: a slot of its own, next to the list.
- The marker is the shape itself (a rounded rect with the meter), not a frame with children: harry moves a marker's own shape.

## #icon

A 24 px glyph (Lucide) for the slots of other components; display only, no state.

### Figma

- set: `#icon` (node 2-961 in the Library)
- property `icon`: `wifi` | `wifi-high` | `wifi-low` | `wifi-zero` | `lock` | `chevron-right` | `minus` | `plus` | `settings-2` | `sliders-horizontal` | `maximize-2`
- variant string: `icon=wifi` (the properties in this order; `Component::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: a glyph, 24 px (Lucide): for the slots of other components; no state
- on the screens now: not used yet
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#icon` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Rust

- no Rust state machine: the app sets the parts directly (texts, opacities, meters)

### The app

No Rust binding yet: the app cannot put `#icon` in a slot (no `impl Slotted` in harry/src/slot.rs).

`icon` names the glyph. The set exists so that a list row, a tile or a symbol can show one of many glyphs by stacking instances at opacity 0 and lighting one: harry does not swap a variant inside a list item, so a row's leading icon is a stack of `#list-item/leading/<glyph>`.

### In Figma
Inside another component's layer, one instance per glyph the place can show, all at opacity 0 but the preview's; named `<part>/<glyph>`. Alone on a screen an icon is a plain picture of the design, not a slot.

### Traps
- A glyph that is not in the stack cannot be shown at runtime; add it to the stack (and to `components.json` for the icon buttons) rather than drawing it on the screen.
- An instance swap at runtime is a variant change in a list item and is ignored by harry: opacity only.

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #segmented

One choice of two to four, Material 3's segmented button: the segments are tap targets, the selected one is lit by opacity.

### Figma

- set: `#segmented` (node 2-1034 in the Library)
- property `segments`: `2` | `3` | `4`
- property `state`: `default` | `disabled`
- variant string: `segments=2, state=default` (the properties in this order; `Segmented::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: Material 3's segmented button, one choice of 2 to 4: per segment #segmented/segment-<i> (a touch target), /selected (the accent highlight), /label (ink2) and /label-selected (white); the choice lights a segment by opacity, the labels set by code; not a variant
- nodes set by code (`Segmented`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#segmented/segment-{}`, `#segmented/segment-<…>`
- on the screens now: `#office/fan` in Room controls (node 1-178)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#segmented` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- value: 160 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/segmented.rs`, type `Segmented`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Segmented`)
- `pub fn new<S: Into<String>>(labels: impl IntoIterator<Item = S>) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, index: usize, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<SegmentedEvent>`
- events `SegmentedEvent`: `Selected(usize)`
- pub struct `Segmented`: A segmented button.
  - field `pub labels: Vec<String>`: The segments' labels, in order (2 to 4).
  - field `pub selected: usize`: Index of the chosen segment.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Enabled, and the last change; a segment's press is in `segments`.
  - `pub fn value(&self) -> &str`: The label of the chosen segment.
  - `pub fn select(&mut self, index: usize)`: Chooses a segment from outside (the device reported it); out of range is ignored.
  - `pub fn target(&self, index: usize) -> f32`: Opacity target of segment `index`'s highlight and white label: 100 chosen, 0 not (the ink2 label takes the rest).
  - `pub fn value_transition(&self) -> Option<Transition>`: How the highlight and the labels move to a new choice.
- pub enum `SegmentedEvent`: What a segmented button reports.
  - `Selected`: The user chose the segment with this index.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::segmented::{Segmented, SegmentedEvent};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub office_fan: Segmented,
// office_fan: Segmented::new(["Low", "Med", "High"]),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
office_fan: Slot = "#office/fan" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.office_fan = slot("#office/fan", &state.office_fan);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
// the segments report by their own names, #segmented/segment-1 ...
_ if node.starts_with("#segmented/segment-") => {
    let n = node["#segmented/segment-".len()..].parse::<usize>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_sub(1));
    if let Some(SegmentedEvent::Selected(i)) = n.and_then(|n| state.office_fan.on(n, gesture)) {
        let _ = i; // yours: state.office_fan.value() is the label
    }
}
```

### Live: `#office/fan` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust

/// The Office fan's mode.

fan: Segmented::new(["Low", "Med", "High"]),

// ui_model.rs:175

// presenter.rs:40

```

`segments` is the number (2, 3, 4), `state` `default` or `disabled`. Each segment is `#segmented/segment-<i>` (a tap target) with `/selected` (the lit background) and `/label`; selection fades, the variant does not change. `on(index, gesture)` takes the segment from the node name and answers `Selected(index)`. The texts of the segments are the app's (`set_labels`).

### In Figma
A slot of the variant's size (the design's width per number of segments) named `#<screen>/<name>` (`#office/fan`) with an instance of `#segmented` of the right `segments`. Labels in the preview are placeholders.

### Traps
- `Tabs` look alike but switch screens; a segmented button picks a value. Do not use one for the other (the set names and the roles differ).
- The taps come by the segment's own name (`#segmented/segment-2`): the match arm in actions.rs starts with the prefix, not the slot's name.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #tabs

The screen's navigation, Material 3's tabs: the active tab is lit by opacity, a tap switches the screen.

### Figma

- set: `#tabs` (node 2-2736 in the Library)
- property `tabs`: `2` | `3` | `4`
- property `state`: `default` | `disabled`
- variant string: `tabs=2, state=default` (the properties in this order; `Component::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: Material 3's tabs, the screen's navigation (a segmented button picks a value, tabs switch screens): per tab #tabs/tab-<i> (a touch target) with #tabs/tab-<i>/selected (the white pill), /label (ink2) and /label-selected (accent, semi bold) lit by opacity, set by code, not a variant; the labels set by code
- on the screens now: `#home/tabs` in #smarthome-root (node 1-11); `#rooms/tabs` in #rooms-screen (state=hidden) (node 5-6)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#tabs` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Rust

- no Rust state machine: the app sets the parts directly (texts, opacities, meters)

### The app

No Rust binding yet: the app cannot put `#tabs` in a slot (no `impl Slotted` in harry/src/slot.rs).

`tabs` is the number, `state` `default` or `disabled`. Each tab is `#tabs/tab-<i>` with `/active` (the indicator and the lit label) and `/label`. The app lights the active tab and shows the screen it stands for; switching is the app's (the tabs report a tap on `#tabs/tab-<i>`). There is no Rust state machine yet: the app sets the opacities directly through the parts.

### In Figma
One slot in the header or the bottom bar, named `#<screen>/tabs` (`#home/tabs`), with an instance of `#tabs` of the right number. Every tab is a screen or a frame of the prototype for designers (figma-design skill); on the device the app draws the screen.

### Traps
- Tabs are not a segmented button: a segmented button picks a value in a widget, tabs change what the whole screen shows.
- A tab's label is a text of the component (`#tabs/tab-<i>/label`): the app writes it, the design's text is a placeholder.

- on the screens now: `#rooms/tile-1` in #rooms-screen (state=hidden) (node 5-10); `#rooms/tile-2` in #rooms-screen (state=hidden) (node 5-12); `#rooms/tile-3` in #rooms-screen (state=hidden) (node 5-14)

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/tile.rs`, type `Tile`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Tile`)
- `pub fn new(kind: TileKind, symbol: SymbolIcon, title: impl Into<String>, subtitle: impl Into<String>) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<TileEvent>`
- events `TileEvent`: `Opened`
- pub enum `TileKind`: The kind property of #tile: the control the card shows.
  - `Toggle`: `toggle`: an on/off device (a light).
  - `Slider`: `slider`: a level (a dimmer).
  - `Segmented`: `segmented`: one of 2 to 4 modes (a fan).
  - `Stepper`: `stepper`: a value with minus and plus (a thermostat), the value in #tile/value.
  - `Image`: `image`: a picture (a camera's last frame) in #tile/image.
  - `pub fn name(self) -> &'static str`: The value of the kind property.
- pub struct `Tile`: A device's card.
  - field `pub kind: TileKind`: 
  - field `pub symbol: SymbolIcon`: The device's symbol: the glyph of the stack that is lit.
  - field `pub title: String`: 
  - field `pub subtitle: String`: 
  - field `pub value: String`: The value text (a slider's level, a stepper's value; empty for the others).
  - field `pub toggle: Toggle`: The toggle's state (kind toggle).
  - field `pub slider: Slider`: The slider's level (kind slider; its track is not touched, any x will do).
  - field `pub segmented: Segmented`: The modes and the chosen one (kind segmented).
  - field `pub image: Option<String>`: The key of a registered picture (kind image, everyware_ui::images).
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Pressed and disabled.
  - field `pub selected: bool`: The chosen card of a ribbon (a horizontal ListView lifts it).
  - `pub fn value(mut self, value: impl Into<String>) -> Self`: The value text.
- pub enum `TileEvent`: What a tile reports.
  - `Opened`: The card was tapped: open the device.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::tile::{Tile, TileEvent, TileKind};
use everyware_ui::symbol::SymbolIcon;

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub rooms_tile_1: Tile,
// rooms_tile_1: Tile::new(TileKind::Slider, SymbolIcon::BedDouble, "Bedroom", "Lights").value("65%"),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
rooms_tile_1: Slot = "#rooms/tile-1" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.rooms_tile_1 = slot("#rooms/tile-1", &state.rooms_tile_1);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
"#rooms/tile-1" => {
    if let Some(TileEvent::Opened) = state.rooms_tile_1.on(gesture) {
        // yours: open the device's sheet
    }
}
```

The whole card is one touch target; the control inside shows the device (`state.rooms_tile_1.toggle`, `.slider`, `.segmented`, `.value`) and takes no taps: the device's sheet changes it.

`kind` is the control the card shows: `toggle` (a light), `slider` (a dimmer), `segmented` (a fan's modes), `stepper` (a value with minus and plus) or `image` (a camera's picture); `state` is `default` or `disabled`. Pressed is `#tile/pressed` faded in. The parts: `#tile/title`, `#tile/subtitle`, `#tile/value`, the symbol stack `#tile/symbol/<icon>` (one lit), `#tile/image`, and the control inside: an instance of the Library's toggle, slider or segmented button, which the binding sets as its own (`#toggle/thumb`, `#slider/fill`, `#segmented/segment-<i>/selected` ...).

The card is one touch target and reports `TileEvent::Opened`; the control in it shows the device and takes no taps. Its layers have the same names in every tile of a screen, so a tap on one could not say which tile it was; the device's sheet changes the value.

### In Figma
A slot of the tile's size (438 x 248) named `#<screen>/<device>` with an instance of `#tile` of the right kind. Texts and the control's position in the preview are placeholders.

### Traps
- A glyph that is not in the stack `#tile/symbol/*` cannot be shown: add it to `#symbol` and the stack (ui-component skill).
- Control parts belong to one kind: `#toggle/*` is only in `kind=toggle`. The binding marks them optional per kind, so the contract test checks them in that kind's variants.
- A control that must take taps (a toggle you flip from the dashboard) is its own slot next to a plain card, not inside a tile.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #skeleton

a placeholder while content loads (Material's skeleton loader): grey shapes where the content will be, a heading bar, four text lines or a 16:9 picture, 440 or 832 wide (wide: a side panel's 880 content less 24 on each side)

### Figma

- set: `#skeleton` (node 2-3007 in the Library)
- property `kind`: `heading` | `text` | `media`
- property `size`: `regular` | `wide`
- variant string: `kind=heading, size=regular` (the properties in this order; `Skeleton::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: a placeholder while content loads (Material's skeleton loader): grey shapes where the content will be, a heading bar, four text lines or a 16:9 picture, 440 or 832 wide (wide: a side panel's 880 content less 24 on each side); a light band (#skeleton/shimmer/1..3, horizontal progress markers with the same travel) sweeps across it while loading (change sweep, repeated from the start), still when not; the app fades it out with change hide when the content shows. Display only: the clone takes no taps
- nodes set by code (`Skeleton`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#skeleton/shimmer/{i}`, `#skeleton/shimmer/<…>`
- on the screens now: `#panel/skeleton-1` in #panel-content (state=default) (node 7-10); `#panel/skeleton-2` in #panel-content (state=default) (node 7-12); `#panel/skeleton-3` in #panel-content (state=default) (node 7-14); `#panel/skeleton-4` in #panel-content (state=default) (node 7-16)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#skeleton` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- hide: 250 ms ease-in
- sweep: 1400 ms linear

### Rust

- module: `core/src/skeleton.rs`, type `Skeleton`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Skeleton`)
- `pub fn new(kind: SkeletonKind, size: SkeletonSize) -> Self`
- pub struct `Skeleton`: A skeleton placeholder: its shape, and since when it is loading (None: still).
  - field `pub kind: SkeletonKind`: What it stands for.
  - field `pub size: SkeletonSize`: How wide it is.
  - field `pub since: Option<Instant>`: Loading since then: the band sweeps; None: the shapes stand still.
  - `pub fn start(&mut self, now: Instant)`: Loading from `now`: the band starts sweeping (a skeleton already loading keeps its phase, so a second call does not make it jump).
  - `pub fn stop(&mut self)`: Loaded (or given up): the band stops.
  - `pub fn is_loading(&self) -> bool`: Whether the band sweeps.
  - `pub fn period() -> Duration`: The length of one pass of the band (components.json, `sweep`).
  - `pub fn sweep_at(&self, now: Instant) -> Option<f32>`: Where the band is at `now`, 0..100 across the skeleton; None when it stands still.

## #keyboard

The on-screen keyboard: rows of keys with a character each, pressed keys fade a layer; one component, not a set.

### Figma

- set: `#keyboard` (node 2-2500 in the Library)
- variant string: `` (the properties in this order; `Keyboard::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: #kbd/<key>/pressed opacity (pressed): set by code; one component, not a set
- nodes set by code (`Keyboard`, harry/src/slot.rs): 
- on the screens now: `#osk/keys` in #keyboard-dock (state=closed) (node 3-38)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#keyboard` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/keyboard.rs`, type `Keyboard`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Keyboard`)
- `pub fn on(&mut self, node: &str, gesture: Gesture, text: &mut String) -> Option<Outcome>`
- pub enum `Row`: The key rows with a character on them, top to bottom.
  - `One`: 10 keys.
  - `Two`: 9 keys.
  - `Three`: 7 keys, between Shift and Delete.
- pub enum `Key`: A key of the keyboard.
  - `Char`: A character key: row and index from 0.
  - `Shift`: Upper case for one letter, or the other symbol page.
  - `Delete`: Removes the last character.
  - `Mode`: 123 / abc.
  - `Space`: A space.
  - `Done`: Finished with the field.
- pub enum `Mode`: What the keys show.
  - `Lower`: Lower-case letters.
  - `Upper`: After Shift, for one character.
  - `Symbols`: Digits and the common symbols.
  - `MoreSymbols`: The other symbols (Shift in Symbols).
- pub struct `Keyboard`: Keyboard state: the mode and which keys are pressed; the text belongs to the field being edited.
  - field `pub mode: Mode`: What the keys show.
  - `pub fn on_key(&mut self, node: &str, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<Key>`: Applies a gesture on a key node: the key shows pressed while the finger is on it and is returned when it is released over it.
  - `pub fn key_nodes() -> Vec<String>`: The key nodes of the component, in the order of the layout.
  - `pub fn label_of(&self, node: &str) -> Option<String>`: The label the code sets on a key node (the character keys, Shift and mode); None for keys whose label is fixed in the design (Delete, space, Done).
  - `pub fn pressed_target(&self, node: &str) -> f32`: Opacity target of the pressed layer of a key node: 100 pressed, 0 not.
  - `pub fn press_transition(&self, node: &str) -> Option<Transition>`: How the pressed layer of a key node fades.
  - `pub fn char_at(&self, row: Row, index: usize) -> Option<char>`: The character on a key in the current mode.
  - `pub fn label(&self, row: Row, index: usize) -> String`: The label of a character key.
  - `pub fn shift_label(&self) -> &'static str`: The label of Shift: what pressing it switches to.
  - `pub fn mode_label(&self) -> &'static str`: The label of the mode key: what pressing it switches to.
  - `pub fn press(&mut self, key: Key, text: &mut String) -> Outcome`: Applies a key to `text`.
- pub enum `Outcome`: What a key press means for the screen around the keyboard.
  - `Edited`: The text or the mode changed.
  - `Done`: Done: the user is finished with the field.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::keyboard::Keyboard;

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub osk_keys: Keyboard,
// osk_keys: Keyboard::default(),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
osk_keys: Slot = "#osk/keys" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.osk_keys = slot("#osk/keys", &state.osk_keys);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
// the keys report by their own names, #kbd/<row>/<i>
_ if node.starts_with("#kbd/") => {
    let mut text = String::new(); // yours: the text of the field being edited
    if let Some(outcome) = state.osk_keys.on(node, gesture, &mut text) {
        let _ = outcome;
    }
}
```

Usually inside the keyboard dock with a form (`Form`), which routes the keys to the focused field.

### Live: `#osk/keys` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// ui_model.rs:268
osk_keys: Slot = "#osk/keys" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:114
model.osk_keys = slot("#osk/keys", &state.osk.keyboard);
```

`#keyboard` has no variants: the keys are `#kbd/<row>/<i>` with `/pressed` (faded in while down) and `/label` (the character of the current mode: letters, shift, symbols). `Keyboard::on(gesture)` takes the key from the node name and answers an `Outcome` (a character, backspace, done, a mode change); the text itself belongs to the field being edited (`Form`, `InputField`). The keyboard sits in the keyboard dock (`#keyboard-dock`), one per screen.

### In Figma
Inside the dock's slot (`#<app>/keys`), an instance of `#keyboard`; every key's label is a text override (static labels survive a rebuild), the pressed layer is in the component.

### Traps
- Keys report by their own names (`#kbd/r1/3`): one keyboard on the screen at a time, or the names collide.
- A label as a renamed inner layer is lost on a variant swap of the dock; labels are text overrides (`labelled()` in the generator).

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #slider

A horizontal slider: the fill and the thumb are meters the code moves, the variant is only the state.

### Figma

- set: `#slider` (node 2-2402 in the Library)
- property `state`: `default` | `pressed` | `disabled`
- variant string: `state=default` (the properties in this order; `Slider::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: #slider/fill progress bar meter, #slider/thumb progress marker meter: set by code, not a variant
- nodes set by code (`Slider`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#slider/fill`, `#slider/thumb`
- on the screens now: `#bedroom/dimmer` in Room controls (node 1-157)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#slider` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- press: 80 ms ease-out
- release: 160 ms ease-out
- value: 80 ms ease-out

### Rust

- module: `core/src/slider.rs`, type `Slider`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for Slider`)
- `pub fn new(value: f32, track_x: f32, track_width: f32) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<SliderEvent>`
- events `SliderEvent`: `Moving(f32)`, `Changed(f32)`
- pub struct `Slider`: A horizontal slider over a track at a known place on the display.
  - field `pub value: f32`: 0..100.
  - field `pub step: f32`: Steps of the value; 0 for none.
  - field `pub track_x: f32`: Display x of the track's start (where the thumb's centre is at 0).
  - field `pub track_width: f32`: Track length on the display (thumb centre travel from 0 to 100).
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Pressed and disabled.
  - `pub fn in_slot(value: f32, slot_x: f32, slot_width: f32) -> Self`: A slider at `value` in a slot whose left edge is `slot_x` on the display and which is `slot_width` wide: the track is inset TRACK_INSET on both sides (the #slider design). The slot's place comes from the design (everyware_ui::design::Sizes::frame), so a slot moved in Figma moves the touch area with it.
  - `pub fn dragging(&self) -> bool`: A finger is on the slider: a value from outside (the device reported one) waits until it is up, or the thumb would jump under the finger.
  - `pub fn value_transition(&self) -> Option<Transition>`: How fill and thumb follow the value: short, so the thumb stays under the finger.
- pub enum `SliderEvent`: What a slider reports.
  - `Moving`: The value while dragging.
  - `Changed`: The value when the finger went up.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::slider::{Slider, SliderEvent};
use everyware_ui::design::Sizes;

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub bedroom_dimmer: Slider,
// bedroom_dimmer: Slider::in_slot(65.0, frame.x, frame.width),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
bedroom_dimmer: Slot = "#bedroom/dimmer" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.bedroom_dimmer = slot("#bedroom/dimmer", &state.bedroom_dimmer);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
"#bedroom/dimmer" => {
    if let Some(SliderEvent::Changed(value)) = state.bedroom_dimmer.on(gesture) {
        let _ = value; // yours: the finger is up; Moving(value) while it drags
    }
}
```

`frame` is where the design puts the slot: `let frame = sizes.frame("#bedroom/dimmer")` with `sizes = Sizes::load(<the .dcf>)` at the start; the touch area follows the design.

### Live: `#bedroom/dimmer` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// state.rs:87
pub dimmer: Slider,
dimmer: Slider::new(65.0, 763.0 + 20.0, 203.0),

// ui_model.rs:173
bedroom_dimmer: Slot = "#bedroom/dimmer" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:38
model.bedroom_dimmer = slot("#bedroom/dimmer", &d.dimmer);

// actions.rs:334
"#bedroom/dimmer" => {
    // the value follows the finger (SliderEvent::Moving) and is in the slider; the
    // device gets it when the finger is up
    if let Some(SliderEvent::Changed(percent)) = d.dimmer.on(gesture) {
        return Some(Control::Dimmer(percent));
    }
}
```

`state` is `default`, `pressed` or `disabled`. The value (0..100) moves `#slider/fill` (a progress bar) and `#slider/thumb` (a progress marker), display-only, so the thumb follows the finger every frame. `on(gesture)` answers `Moving(value)` while the finger drags and `Changed(value)` when it lifts; the app sends the device the `Changed` value and may show `Moving` live. `Slider::new(value, track_x, track_width)` needs the track's place on the display, because the finger's x is a display coordinate.

### In Figma
A slot of the slider's size named `#<screen>/<name>` (`#bedroom/dimmer`) with an instance of `#slider`; the thumb marker at x = 0 of the track, its travel the track's width. The app's `track_x`/`track_width` are the slot's x and width in the design.

### Traps
- A thumb that starts in the wrong place or runs past the end: the marker node is not at x = 0 of its parent, or startX..endX is not the travel.
- The value changes but nothing moves: the marker must be the shape itself (a rounded rect), not a frame with children.
- A slider moved to another x in Figma needs the new `track_x` in the app: `everyware_ui_test` cannot see it, the finger can.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)

### Live: `#weather/chart` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust

// presenter.rs:139

```

`#bar-chart` has one variant, `bars=24`: `#bar-chart/bar/<1..24>` are vertical progress bar meters (the level, 0..100), `#bar-chart/bar/<i>/accent` is the same bar in the accent colour, shown by opacity. `BarChart::new(bars)` takes (level, accent) pairs; it clamps a level to 0..100 and does nothing else. Scaling data to levels (a day's temperatures to the chart's height) and choosing the accented bars (the hours with rain) is the app's presenter.

### In Figma

### Traps

### Check
