## <app>-sheet

The state machine of anything shown over the screen: closed or open, with the open and close transitions; the base of Sheet and Form.

### Figma

- set: `<app>-sheet`
- property `state`: `closed` | `open`
- variant string: `state=closed` (the properties in this order; `Overlay::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: an overlay over the screen: the variant is the state, harry animates the change with the open/close transitions; one set per overlay in the app's design. The moving parts carry the same animation as the instance: harry gives a variant change's children no animation of their own
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `<app>-sheet` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- open: 550 ms spring
- close: 400 ms spring

### Rust

- module: `core/src/overlay.rs`, type `Overlay`
- `pub fn new() -> Self`
- pub struct `Overlay`: An overlay: closed or open.
  - field `pub open: bool`: Shown over the dashboard.
  - `pub fn open(&mut self)`: Opens it; the change animates with the open transition.
  - `pub fn close(&mut self)`: Closes it; the change animates with the close transition.
  - `pub fn slide(&self, open: f32, closed: f32) -> f32`: Where a part that moves with the overlay goes: `open` while it is open, `closed` while it is closed (a card's y in the open drawing and below the screen, a scrim's opacity).
  - `pub fn transition(&self) -> Option<Transition>`: The transition of the last change (open or close), for harry's animation of the variant.

`Overlay` is not a Figma set of its own: it is the Rust side of `#sheet` and of the keyboard dock. `open()`, `close()`, `is_open()`, `transition()` (the `open` or `close` spec from components.json for the change that just happened). A sheet or a dialog is `Sheet` (sheet.rs), which adds the layout; a sheet with input fields is `Form` (form.rs).

### In Figma
Nothing: see `#sheet`.

### Traps
- The app moves the card and fades the scrim from the overlay's state (display-only); it never sets the sheet instance's variant.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## <app>-sheet

A sheet with input fields: a tap focuses a field, the screen's keyboard dock opens and types into it, Enter submits.

### Figma

- set: `<app>-sheet`
- property `state`: `closed` | `open`
- variant string: `state=closed` (the properties in this order; `Form::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: an overlay with input fields (slots): a tap focuses a field, the screen's keyboard dock opens and types into it; one set per form in the app's design, state first
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `<app>-sheet` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- open: 550 ms spring
- close: 400 ms spring

### Rust

- module: `core/src/form.rs`, type `Form`
- `pub fn new(layout: Layout, fields: impl IntoIterator<Item = (impl Into<String>, InputField)>) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, node: &str, gesture: Gesture, now: Instant, keyboard: &mut Keyboard) -> Option<FormEvent>`
- events `FormEvent`: `Focused(usize)`, `Edited(usize)`, `Submitted(usize)`
- pub struct `Form`: A sheet with input fields.
  - field `pub sheet: Sheet`: The sheet: closed or open over the screen, its layout, the card's place.
  - `pub fn open(&mut self)`: Opens it, nothing in focus; the change animates with the open transition.
  - `pub fn close(&mut self)`: Closes it and takes the focus away (the keyboard closes with it); the change animates with the close transition.
  - `pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool`: Whether the sheet is open.
  - `pub fn clear(&mut self)`: Empties the fields (texts and errors); placeholders and helpers stay.
  - `pub fn field(&self, index: usize) -> &InputField`: A field, by its index in `new`.
  - `pub fn field_mut(&mut self, index: usize) -> &mut InputField`: A field to change, by its index in `new`.
  - `pub fn focused(&self) -> Option<usize>`: The field with the focus; the keyboard dock follows it.
  - `pub fn focus(&mut self, index: usize, now: Instant)`: Gives a field the focus; a disabled field does not take it.
  - `pub fn blur(&mut self)`: Takes the focus away from every field.
- pub enum `FormEvent`: What the form reports; the index is the field's, in the order given to `new`.
  - `Focused`: A tap gave a field the focus (the keyboard opens).
  - `Edited`: A key changed a field's text.
  - `Submitted`: Done on the keyboard: the field's text is submitted.

`Form::new(layout, fields)` wraps a `Sheet` and the fields' `InputField`s, in the order given. `on(node, gesture, now, keyboard)` routes a tap to the field by its node name and the keyboard's outcome to the focused field; it answers `Focused(i)`, `Edited(i)`, `Submitted(i)`. The keyboard dock follows the focus: `state.osk.follow(form.focused().is_some())` after every action.

### In Figma
The fields are slots of `#input-field` inside the sheet's content component (`#wifi/password`); the form is code.

### Traps
- A dialog with a form moves above the keyboard dock (the free height); a side panel does not.
- The field's text is the form's, not the keyboard's: the keyboard only reports outcomes.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #keyboard-dock

The screen's one keyboard: an overlay at the bottom with the keyboard component in its slot, open while a field has the focus.

### Figma

- set: `#keyboard-dock` (node 3-36 in the Library)
- property `state`: `closed` | `open`
- variant string: `state=closed` (the properties in this order; `KeyboardDock::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: the screen's one keyboard: an overlay at the bottom with the #keyboard component in its slot (#<app>/keys), open while a field has the focus; the slot moves with the dock's animation
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#keyboard-dock` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- open: 550 ms spring
- close: 400 ms spring

### Rust

- module: `core/src/dock.rs`, type `KeyboardDock`
- `pub fn new() -> Self`
- pub struct `KeyboardDock`: The screen's keyboard: an overlay with the keys.
  - field `pub overlay: Overlay`: Closed (below the screen) or open (docked at the bottom).
  - field `pub keyboard: Keyboard`: The keys: labels per mode, pressed keys, typing.
  - `pub fn follow(&mut self, focus: bool)`: Opens the dock while a field has the focus and closes it when none has: the screen calls it after every action with `form.focused().is_some()` (or several forms' or'ed).
  - `pub fn open(&self) -> bool`: The dock is open: the keys are on the screen.

`state` is `closed` or `open`; the dock slides up by the `open` transition and is 420 px high (`KEYBOARD_DOCK_H`). `KeyboardDock::follow(focused)` opens and closes it with the focus; `keyboard` inside it is the `Keyboard` state machine. One dock per screen, above every sheet.

### In Figma
A plain absolute frame over the screen with an instance of `#keyboard-dock` (state `closed`, below the screen's edge) whose slot `#<app>/keys` holds `#keyboard`; the last layer of the root so it is above the sheets.

### Traps
- An instance placed absolute by itself lands in the root's flow after import: the instance inside a plain frame with absolute positioning.
- Dialogs centre in the screen minus the dock while it is open: give the presenter the free height (`SCREEN.1 - KEYBOARD_DOCK_H`).

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #input-field

A one-line text field: the focus ring, the caret and the placeholder are opacities, the variant is only the state.

### Figma

- set: `#input-field` (node 2-2473 in the Library)
- property `state`: `default` | `disabled` | `error`
- variant string: `state=default` (the properties in this order; `InputField::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: #input-field/focus opacity (focused), #input-field/caret blinks by opacity, #input-field/placeholder opacity (empty), texts: set by code, not a variant
- nodes set by code (`InputField`, harry/src/slot.rs): `#input-field/text`, `#input-field/placeholder`, `#input-field/helper`, `#input-field/focus`, `#input-field/caret`
- on the screens now: `#wifi/password` in #wifi-content (step=password) (node 3-30)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#input-field` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- focus: 150 ms ease-out
- blur: 150 ms ease-in

### Rust

- module: `core/src/input_field.rs`, type `InputField`; binding: `harry/src/slot.rs` (`impl Slotted for InputField`)
- `pub fn new(placeholder: impl Into<String>, helper: impl Into<String>) -> Self`
- `pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture, now: Instant) -> Option<InputEvent>`
- events `InputEvent`: `Focused`
- pub struct `InputField`: A one-line text field.
  - field `pub text: String`: The text the user entered.
  - field `pub placeholder: String`: Shown while the text is empty.
  - field `pub helper: String`: Shown under the field while there is no error.
  - field `pub error: Option<String>`: An error: the field turns red and shows it instead of the helper.
  - field `pub secure: bool`: Shows dots instead of the characters (passwords).
  - field `pub focused: bool`: Takes the keyboard's input.
  - field `pub press: Pressable`: Disabled; taps do not focus it.
  - `pub fn focus(&mut self, now: Instant)`: Takes the focus (the keyboard writes here).
  - `pub fn blur(&mut self)`: Gives the focus away.
  - `pub fn edited(&mut self, now: Instant)`: The text was changed (by the keyboard): the caret restarts on, an error goes away.
  - `pub fn shown(&self) -> String`: The text to show: dots for a secure field.
  - `pub fn helper_line(&self) -> &str`: The line under the field: the error, else the helper.
  - `pub fn focus_target(&self) -> f32`: Opacity target of the focus ring: 100 focused, 0 not.
  - `pub fn focus_transition(&self) -> Option<Transition>`: How the ring fades: focus and blur have their own curves.
  - `pub fn placeholder_target(&self) -> f32`: Opacity target of the placeholder: 100 while the text is empty.
  - `pub fn caret_since(&self) -> Option<Instant>`: Since when the caret blinks; none while not focused (no caret).
  - `pub fn caret_on(&self, now: Instant) -> bool`: Whether the caret is on at `now`: on for BLINK_MS, off for BLINK_MS, from `caret_since`.
- pub enum `InputEvent`: What an input field reports.
  - `Focused`: A tap focused it.

### The app: the lines per component on the screen (compiled by everyware_ui_recipes_test)

```rust
// imports
use everyware_ui::input_field::{InputEvent, InputField};

// state.rs: in struct State, and its first value in State::new
pub wifi_password: InputField,
// wifi_password: InputField::new("Password", ""),

// ui_model.rs: in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... } (the contract with the design)
wifi_password: Slot = "#wifi/password" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs: after every action
model.wifi_password = slot("#wifi/password", &state.wifi_password);

// actions.rs: in the match on the gesture's node name
"#wifi/password" => {
    if let Some(InputEvent::Focused) = state.wifi_password.on(gesture, Instant::now()) {
        // yours: open the keyboard (a Form does it for its fields)
    }
}
```

### Live: `#wifi/password` in smarthome-app (cut from the sources at build time)

```rust
// ui_model.rs:212
wifi_password: Slot = "#wifi/password" ["SlotCustomizer"];

// presenter.rs:64
model.wifi_password = slot("#wifi/password", wifi.password());
```

`state` is `default`, `disabled` or `error`. Focus (`#input-field/focus`), the blinking caret (`#input-field/caret`), the placeholder (`#input-field/placeholder`, shown while empty) are opacities; the text is `#input-field/text` (dots while `secure`). `InputField::new(placeholder, helper)`; `on(gesture, now)` answers `Focused`; typing comes through the `Form` from the keyboard.

### In Figma
A slot of the field's size named `#<screen>/<name>` (`#wifi/password`) with an instance of `#input-field`; the text node carries at least a space as preview (an empty text may be dropped on import).

### Traps
- Text wrapping one character per line, or a focus ring that never shows, is stock harry's list-item bug; the display_safety series in `everyware/patches` fixes both.
- The caret blinks through `UpdatePolicy` from the binding: nothing to animate in the app.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)


## #sheet

The container for anything over the screen, Material 3's dialog and side sheet, with the app's content component in its slot.

### Figma

- set: `#sheet` (node 2-2963 in the Library)
- property `layout`: `dialog` | `left` | `right` | `top` | `bottom`
- property `state`: `closed` | `open`
- variant string: `layout=dialog, state=closed` (the properties in this order; `Sheet::variant()` produces it, never typed by hand)
- parts the code sets: the library's container for anything over the screen: #sheet/scrim (opacity 0 to 35 %) and #sheet/card, a dialog 1120 wide in the middle, as high as its content plus 40 around it (the card hugs the content; the app reads the content's height from the .dcf, design.rs), or a panel along an edge, half the screen; #sheet/content is an empty slot for the app's content. The app gives the card its position (FollowPositionCustomizer, ui-lib sheet.rs: the closed card waits 40 px behind its edge, a dialog is centred by its content's height) and the scrim its opacity, so open and close are display-only; the app never sets the instance's variant (the Library's variant has no content)
- to place one: a frame named `#<screen>/<name>` with an instance of `#sheet` inside (the slot); texts in it are placeholders, nothing hidden

### Transitions (components.json, through `transition()`)

- open: 550 ms spring
- close: 400 ms spring

### Rust

- module: `core/src/sheet.rs`, type `Sheet`
- `pub fn new(layout: Layout) -> Self`
- pub enum `Edge`: The screen's edge a panel sits at and slides in from.
  - `Left`: 
  - `Right`: 
  - `Top`: 
  - `Bottom`: 
- pub enum `Layout`: How a sheet shows its card.
  - `Dialog`: A card in the middle of the screen, in from the bottom.
  - `Panel`: A panel along `Edge`, half the screen, in from behind that edge.
  - `pub fn name(self) -> &'static str`: The value of the Figma property `layout`.
  - `pub fn card(self, screen: (f32, f32), content_height: Option<f32>) -> Rect`: The card open, on a screen of `(w, h)`, with the content `content_height` high (a dialog's card hugs it; None: the default height).
  - `pub fn closed(self, screen: (f32, f32)) -> (f32, f32)`: Where the card waits closed: behind the edge it comes from, `CLOSED_GAP` past the screen.
- pub struct `Sheet`: A sheet: an overlay with the library's card, in one of the layouts.
  - field `pub overlay: Overlay`: 
  - field `pub layout: Layout`: 
  - field `pub content_height: Option<f32>`: The height of the content in the card (design.rs Sizes): the card hugs it, so the middle of the screen depends on it. None until known: the default dialog height.
  - `pub fn with_content_height(mut self, height: Option<f32>) -> Self`: The same sheet with this content height (the card's height follows the content).
  - `pub fn open(&mut self)`: 
  - `pub fn close(&mut self)`: 
  - `pub fn is_open(&self) -> bool`: 
  - `pub fn card_position(&self, screen: (f32, f32), free_height: f32) -> (f32, f32)`: Where the card is now: in place while open, behind its edge while closed; the app gives both coordinates to the card as a position override (FollowPositionCustomizer). `free_height`: the screen's height without what covers its bottom (the keyboard dock while it is open): a dialog is centred in that, or at the top when it is higher than that, as a phone moves a dialog above its keyboard. A panel keeps its edge.
  - `pub fn scrim(&self) -> f32`: The scrim's opacity, 0..100.
  - `pub fn transition(&self) -> Option<Transition>`: 

`layout` is where the card is: `dialog` (1120 wide in the middle, in from the bottom, as high as its content) or a panel along an edge (`left`, `right`: half the width and the full height; `top`, `bottom`: the full width and half the height). `state` is `closed` (the card 40 px behind its edge, the scrim clear) or `open`. The parts: `#sheet/scrim`, `#sheet/card`, `#sheet/content`, a slot that holds the content component.

The app **never sets a sheet's variant**: harry would take the variant from the Library and the instance's own part names and content would be lost. The instance stays the closed variant of the design; the app slides the card from behind its edge and fades the scrim, both display-only.

### In Figma
Three things make a sheet in the design:

1. **The content**: a component of the app's design (`#wifi-content`, `#device-content`, …), set to auto layout that **hugs** one inner frame of the content's size, with the app's layers inside that frame (`#wifi/networks`, `#wifi/password`, the buttons' slots). A step or mode of the sheet is a variant property of this component (`step=networks|password`).
2. **The sheet on the screen**: an instance of the library's `#sheet` (`layout=dialog`, or a panel edge; `state=closed`) in a plain frame over the whole screen. Select its nested `#sheet/content` and **swap the instance** to the content component. Rename the three parts in the instance for this sheet: `#sheet/scrim` → `#<x>/scrim`, `#sheet/card` → `#<x>/card`, `#sheet/content` → `#<x>/content`, so the app can drive each sheet by its own names.
3. **Nothing hidden and nothing resized by hand**: the card hugs the content (a dialog's height follows it), the closed variant keeps the card behind the screen's edge; the app slides it in.

The sheets the app has now (#wifi, #device, #panel) are built exactly like this; the designer frames below the dashboard show each one open.

### In the app
```rust
// state: the sheet (or a Form: a sheet with input fields) and its layout
pub const WIFI_LAYOUT: Layout = Layout::Dialog;
pub const PANEL_LAYOUT: Layout = Layout::Panel(Edge::Right);
pub panel: Sheet,                                        // Sheet::new(PANEL_LAYOUT)
form: Form::new(WIFI_LAYOUT, [("#wifi/password", password)]),

// ui_model: the card moves on both axes, the scrim fades and takes taps while open
panel_card: Position = "#panel/card" ["FollowPositionCustomizer"] = Position::new(PANEL_LAYOUT.closed(SCREEN), None);
panel_scrim: Meter = "#panel/scrim" ["FollowOpacityCustomizer"] = Meter::new(0.0, None);
panel_scrim_taps: TapTarget = "#panel/scrim" ["TapTargetCustomizer"];
_panel_card_tap: () = "#panel/card" interactive;         // a tap on the card stays on the card
wifi_step: Variant = "#wifi/content" = Variant("step=networks".to_string());   // a step is the content's variant

// presenter: the content's height from the design (Sizes, read from the .dcf at the start)
// centres a dialog; while the keyboard dock is open, in the screen above it
let free_height = if state.osk.open() { SCREEN.1 - KEYBOARD_DOCK_H } else { SCREEN.1 };
let sheet = wifi.form.sheet.with_content_height(state.sizes.height("#wifi-content", &wifi.step_variant()));
let slide = wifi.form.transition();
model.wifi_card = Position::new(sheet.card_position(SCREEN, free_height), slide);
model.wifi_scrim = Meter::new(sheet.scrim(), slide);
model.wifi_scrim_taps = TapTarget(wifi.form.is_open());

// actions: open from a tap, close from the scrim or a button
state.panel.open();
"#wifi/scrim" if matches!(gesture, Gesture::Up { inside: true, .. }) => wifi.form.close(),
```

### Traps
- Setting `Variant` on the sheet instance shows every sheet open and empty: the Library's variant has no content and the names `#sheet/*`.
- A size override on the nested content instance is not honoured by Figma's import; the content component hugs a box instead (`hugBox`).
- A dialog higher than the screen above the keyboard sits at the top; a panel never moves for the keyboard.

### Check

- `everyware_ui_test` (host): the variants and parts the code uses exist in the app's .dcf
- `scripts/check.sh` before the commit: tests, coverage, this file regenerated (`node docs/build-docs.js`)
